newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary bonds seen stable,awaiting inflation plans.
newsitem.headline: Hungary bonds seen stable,awaiting inflation plans.

text.p: Hungarian dealers said they did not expect large changes in government bond yields on the secondary market this week
They added that the market waited for signals from the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) and the Finance Ministry about their interest rate and inflation policies.
"There is not large activity this week," said Tamas Puskas of Raiffeisen Securities. "Almost everybody has been trying to get to short-term securities (Treasury bills) and they are waiting now."

Dealers expected slight rises in yields at the auctions of two-year and five-year government bond auctions on Thursday but they said this was not likely to change yields on the secondary market substantially.
They said the rising trend in government bond yields, triggered by an NBH rate hike one month ago, could continue for the short term, but at a slow pace.
Dealers said expectations for a declining trend in yields and for repo cuts were reappearing on the markets.
"In the near future, the yields will move downward, as the papers already have fairly high real yields," said Zsolt Bango of Gog Securities said.
Dealers said the markets were looking at the Finance Ministry and the NBH which are expected to prepare a plan for a radical inflation cut in 1998 by the end of April.
"The expectation is that the NBH will soften its interest rate policy," Puskas said. "I think it should be a part of an anti-inflationary package that interest rates are allowed to drop."
